key_insight: First-principles calculations predict that full hydrogenation converts metallic irida-graphene into irida-graphane, an indirect wide-band-gap semiconductor with a 6.0 eV HSE06 gap.
engineering_relevance: Predicted visible transparency and strong deep-ultraviolet absorption make irida-graphane a candidate for UV optoelectronics and transparent coatings.
method: PBE and HSE06 density functional theory for structural, electronic, and optical properties.
Phonon calculations and ab initio molecular dynamics for stability.
Mechanical response calculations for stiffness, isotropy, and critical strain.
evidence_signal: Calculations show no imaginary phonon frequencies, structural integrity during AIMD simulations up to 2000 K, visible reflectivity below 0.3%, and deep-UV absorption coefficients of 10^5–10^6 cm⁻¹.
watch_item: The predictions require experimental validation, particularly synthesis with complete hydrogenation and confirmation of stability and optical performance.
paper_title: First-Principles Investigation of Irida-Graphane: A Wide-Band-Gap Semiconductor Derived from Irida-Graphene
